It is often stated that Voat is based in Switzerland, and the FAQ Page hints that Voat is at least under Swiss jurisdiction.

So I poked around the Swiss commercial register a bit looking for companies containing "voat" or "whoaverse", but couldn't find anything.

Whois didn't help, because Voat uses WhoisGuard.

Since Voat™ is apparently a registered trademark, I also looked in the Swiss trademark register, but couldn't find anything either.

There's also no indication that Voat itself is hosted in Switzerland. The old hoster, hosteurope.de, is an UK/German company.

The new hoster seems to be Cloudflare Inc., which is an US company (which I find a bit worrying, btw).

So, what does "Voat is based in Switzerland" mean, and how does Swiss law apply to its content?

Edit: Even The Guardian calls Voat a "Swiss clone" of reddit, without further going into detail about the Swiss part.
I'm certainly curious; more for curiosity's sake than malice or sensationalism.

Cloudflare isn't a web host, it's a proxy service that helps protect sites from DDoS attacks (among other things). The fact that Cloudflare is based in the U.S. has no bearing on voat's content or legalities.

CloudFlare has data centers all over the world: https://www.cloudflarestatus.com

None in Switzerland, though. Tracing the IP of their servers takes you to San Francisco.

Clearly they are in the processing of applying for and getting all the official documentation and registrations together. Just a few weeks ago they were trying to survive a massive influx of new users and then a DDOS. If it was me the paperwork might be let to slide while the major fires got put out (ok, maybe not the legal documents for an LLC or equivalent to provide liability protection).
